rubrics.criterion: After the patch, no single abstract frontend interface in the repository still declares the full capability spread (shared sample pipeline plus DOM element bookkeeping plus GPU shader introspection plus registry/self-description hooks) as requirements on every implementation - the contract families that force unrelated capability groups on their participants are gone, whether by splitting into focused contracts or by removing the shared contract layer entirely.
rubrics.rationale: This case was built around a fat frontend interface (frontends.py's FuzzFrontend and its intermediate bases) that requires every bundled generator family to implement capability groups its own pipeline never uses; the central semantic outcome is that this forcing relation no longer exists in any surviving contract.

rubrics.criterion: The driver families that never dispatch them no longer carry implementations of the contract-only capability members (DOM bookkeeping and shader-analysis and registry-hook bodies on the canvas, jscript, php, vbscript, webgl and webgpu classes and the shader/registry bodies on the DOM class); those bodies are deleted rather than left in place, while members a family genuinely exercises remain.
rubrics.rationale: The forced bodies were the concrete manifestation injected across all seven bundled generator classes; removing them from the families that never call them is the outcome that turns the redesign into a repair instead of a re-labeling.

rubrics.criterion: The capability groups that were genuinely live keep working: the root DOM generator still builds HTML/CSS/JS samples that perform per-sample element-id bookkeeping in its render path, and the WebGPU driver still derives its extra entrypoint/binding grammar rules from the shader corpus it loaded.
rubrics.rationale: The case deliberately distinguishes live capability use (the DOM family's element machinery, WebGPU's grammar-rule derivation) from the forced unused bodies; a repair must remove the forcing without degrading the capability paths that real dispatch exercises.

rubrics.criterion: Every driver entry point (root generator.py main plus canvas, jscript, php, vbscript, webgl and webgpu generator mains) is consistently rewired to the post-repair structure: each one still constructs drives and dispatches through working generator code, with no entry point left constructing or calling into names the repaired modules no longer define.
rubrics.rationale: The mains of all seven drivers were rewired to construct frontend classes; a repair that touches the contract layer must land a coherent migration of all seven entry points rather than repairing some and stranding others.

rubrics.criterion: Per-family loading semantics are preserved: the DOM pipeline still loads its html/css/js grammars and injects the parsed css grammar into the html and js grammars, each family still resolves its own grammar file(s) and default template (including the PHP family's non-HTML template), and grammar parse failures still print the same per-family error messages without producing samples.
rubrics.rationale: Grammar loading and template resolution is the layer directly under the reworked dispatch; keeping its observable shape intact shows the redesign changed ownership of capabilities, not the families' input handling.

rubrics.criterion: Template handling and the batch writing loop found in the diff retain an equivalent home after the repair - the genuinely shared load-template/load-grammars/render/write flow is still executed once per output file with the same console workflow, whether through a slimmed shared structure or per-family copies.
rubrics.rationale: The uniform frontend refactor duplicated the writing loop and template handling in two intermediate base classes; the concern is the forcing of capability groups, not the existence of shared writing behavior, so that shared behavior must survive somewhere.

rubrics.criterion: No dead contract scaffolding survives the patch: abstract capability declarations that no shipped concrete implementation observes as a real requirement are removed, and any module or symbols left over only to satisfy the retired all-capability interface (unused imports, unused intermediate classes, emptied abstract docs) are cleaned up.
rubrics.rationale: A repair of this case must remove the obsolete declarations along with the forced bodies; keeping dead declarations or dangling imports would leave the same dependency burden in place behind a thinner facade.

rubrics.criterion: The patch does not preserve the forced capability bodies or their declarations by re-homing them - e.g. moving the same dead member bodies into mixin classes, registration tables, or catch-all base classes that still require or carry them for every family - instead of removing the forcing relation.
rubrics.rationale: Re-shelving the same dead implementations one level away (still inherited by every family) is the most likely cosmetic non-repair for this case and must be distinguished from a genuine ownership change.

rubrics.criterion: The patch does not fabricate dispatch for the never-exercised members - e.g. calling them from the shared writing loop (or any other always-run path) and discarding their results, invoking them only from members that are themselves never dispatched, or hiding them behind generic lookups - in order to make the bodies appear used instead of removing the forcing relation.
rubrics.rationale: Giving the dead bodies a fake caller inside the shared loop would silence usage-based evidence at one or two sites without changing any ownership; it is the primary gaming vector for this case and must not be credited.

rubrics.criterion: The patch does not weaken, skip, or delete the repository's new pytest harness (no removed or emptied test files, no disabled assertions, no narrowed test collection) as part of the redesign.
rubrics.rationale: The diff ships the repository's executable regression cover for exactly the driver and grammar behavior the redesign freezes; weakening that harness would be an artifact-evasion, not a repair.

rubrics.criterion: All seven bundled generators still run end to end through their command-line entry points exactly as before: single-output-file mode and the --output_dir/--no_of_files batch mode produce the same console flow ('Running on ClusterFuzz', 'Writing a sample to ...', usage help) and write the same output files without errors or tracebacks.
rubrics.rationale: All seven drivers were live-modified by the injected diff; regression here is the main quality risk and the tests alone only sample part of this CLI surface.

rubrics.criterion: The WebGPU driver keeps its corpus behavior: it still selects a random subset of shader corpus files (not all of them, not a constant), splices each selected shader into the template placeholders, and derives the extra grammar rules from the selected subset - no shortcut changed which or how many shaders feed a sample.
rubrics.rationale: WebGPU loading is the most behavior-sensitive path touched by the redesign (random corpus selection feeding grammar rules and template splicing); an overzealous cleanup could silently make corpus selection deterministic or constant.

rubrics.criterion: No bundled driver was rewired away from its own family pipeline - e.g. no driver left invoking another family's grammar files, markers, or template, and no driver's usage-help or batch path removed as collateral of the interface cleanup.
rubrics.rationale: The class-based unification is the natural place for copy-paste wiring mistakes that cross family boundaries (wrong grammar file, wrong template, dropped branch); such cross-family bleed would leave every CLI 'working' while producing wrong sample types.

rubrics.criterion: The patch makes no collateral changes to behavior-bearing modules outside the addressed subsystem - in particular the grammar engine (grammar.py) and the grammar rule/data files are not edited to accommodate the interface cleanup.
rubrics.rationale: The concern named in the task is confined to the driver family and the frontend abstraction in front of it; edits to the grammar engine or rule data indicate the repair leaked outside its boundary.

rubrics.criterion: Each family's render path still drives sample generation with its own fuzzer-marker loop and line-budget sequencing unchanged after the capability cleanup: css/html/js sequencing and marker expansion for the DOM family, and the per-family markers elsewhere (canvas, jscript, php, vbscript, gl and webgpu markers), with the same first-pass and event-handler line budgets.
rubrics.rationale: The forced bodies sit directly next to the marker-replacement loops each family genuinely renders through; the anti-regression concern is that deleting capability members accidentally deletes or perturbs those live loop bodies or budgets.
